targets.title: The bounds of adult language acquisition: Blocking and learned attention
targets.evidence_quote:
It replicates and extends Ellis and
Sagarra (2010) in demonstrating short- and long-term learned attention in the acquisition of temporal reference in Latin.
targets.outcome_quote:
The present study demonstrates this replicability: The
experiments once again show that the early stages of adult language
learning are sensitive to blocking effects from varying sequences of cue
exposure and to L1 background (here with a greater range of L1s).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The conclusion explicitly states that the present study demonstrates replicability across the experiments, covering instructional blocking and L1 background. This overall verdict governs despite described changes in control-group cue biases and reduced blocking of salient adverbs.

reasoning: Two new-sample experiments replicate and extend the two experiments in one published 2010 paper. The accompanying synthesis does not add replication targets.
